## What's Changed

- **Dev Machines without XFS (monitored disk mode):** Set `DEV_MACHINE_DISK_QUOTA_MODE=monitored` to run Dev Machines on hosts whose Docker data root has no XFS project quotas (for example ext4). Workspace disk limits are then measured every 30 seconds instead of enforced by the kernel. Machines warn at 90 %, stop at 100 %, and all machines stop (with new starts refused) when the host's free space falls below a configurable floor. Administrators see a banner in Dev Machine settings, and machine pages label the limit as monitored. Hard mode remains the default.
- **Custom machine sizes:** Choose vCPU, memory and disk with sliders that snap to sensible values, instead of fixed Small/Medium/Large presets. Memory stays at least 1 GB per vCPU and disk within the workspace limit. Environment Builders now open the same resource dialog.
- **Clearer limits:** Machines that never started and are no longer wanted no longer count towards workspace or per-user limits. Quota errors say which limit was reached and how to proceed.
- **Disk usage visibility:** Machine pages highlight workspace disk usage at 90 % or more of the limit.

## Upgrade Notes

- Migration `000048` allows the new `custom` machine size; its rollback converts custom machines to `large`.
- The self-hosting Compose file now mounts Docker's data root read-only into the machine manager (`DEV_MACHINE_DOCKER_ROOT`, default `/var/lib/docker`) and passes `DEV_MACHINE_DISK_QUOTA_MODE`, `DEV_MACHINE_HOST_DISK_MIN_FREE_PERCENT` (15) and `DEV_MACHINE_HOST_DISK_MIN_FREE_GB` (25).
- Existing installations stay in hard mode unless they opt in. In monitored mode a fast writer can briefly exceed its limit between checks, so size the free-space floor to absorb that.

[PR #81](https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/81) · [Disk limitation docs](https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/blob/main/TECHNICAL.md#disk-limitation)

## Validation

PR #81 passed all of its CI jobs on `824d070`, including:
- backend tests against PostgreSQL;
- Docker runtime integration;
- every Dev Machine image and every release image (amd64 and arm64);
- the frontend, Go and updater security scans;
- self-hosting checks.

UI: 42 unit tests and 144 browser tests. Candidate `277d7ae` (the merge commit on `main`) passed the full Tests and Security Scan runs. The publishing workflow updates version files on `main`. If its resulting commit differs from this candidate, revalidate that commit before rollout.

## What's Changed

- **Original UI design restored (KUA-63):** Buttons, fields and selects migrated in v0.1.25 regain their original size, padding, alignment, colors and hover states. They still use the shared shadcn-svelte foundation, through a new opt-in `plain` variant.
- **Sidebar:** Team rows and section headings are left-aligned with navigation again. Expanded sections no longer show a permanent grey highlight, and keyboard focus wraps the whole header row as before. Drag-reorder and the collapsed drawer are unchanged.
- **Issue lists:** Group headers lose the new grey bars and thick focus ring. Clicking anywhere in the checkbox area selects an issue, including Shift-click ranges, instead of opening it. Rows are keyboard-focusable again.
- **Issue title:** The issue-creation title is back to its prominent, borderless 18px style.
- **Login and password fields:** The reveal (eye) toggle is vertically centered in every password field and is skipped when tabbing. The Sign in button is back to full height in the accent color.
- **Selects and dialogs:** Selects keep their original look and show their prompt (for example "Choose a workspace member") again. Dialogs return to their original background and overlay without blur. Date pickers follow the app language again.
- **Security:** DOMPurify is updated to 3.4.17 for GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7.
- **CI reliability:** The private-team concurrency test now runs in its own migrated database. Parallel test packages can no longer queue the shared privacy lock and make it time out.

## Upgrade Notes

This release adds no database migrations or required configuration changes compared with v0.1.25. Small visual differences remain from the earlier design: icons redrawn in the Lucide 1.61 update, the centered password toggle, and the removed cycle date-range "×", which never cleared dates.

## What's Changed

- **Consistent application controls (KUA-62):** Inputs, buttons, selects, checkboxes and related controls across Kuayle and its marketing site now use the shared shadcn-svelte foundation. Custom option lists preserve numeric values and form validation.
- **Keyboard and focus improvements:** Selector triggers avoid nested buttons; dialogs, date pickers, machine choices and cookie preferences use accessible primitives. Password reveal actions are keyboard reachable.
- **Updated UI foundation:** Refresh shadcn-svelte components and supporting Svelte, Bits UI, Tailwind and icon packages. Preserve existing dialog positioning, editor uploads, terminal behavior and previously saved team icons.
- **Implementation guidance (KUA-61):** Add repository skills for frontend work, testing, worktrees and review, plus a control audit to help keep future UI work consistent.

- **CI feedback:** Pull requests now run checks for affected areas with stable result gates; main and release validation retain full coverage.

## Upgrade Notes

This release adds no database migrations or required configuration changes compared with v0.1.24. Editor and terminal internals retain their library-managed native elements.

## What's Changed

* **GitHub issue-link bot (KUA-60):** Newly opened pull requests, including drafts and PRs opened by agents, receive a bot comment linking to their associated Kuayle issue. References in the branch, title, and description must resolve to one public-team issue; ambiguous and private issues are skipped.
* **Reliable comment delivery:** Duplicate and concurrent webhook deliveries reconcile existing bot comments before posting. Redelivery preserves later user status changes. Publication respects team privacy without holding database row locks during GitHub requests.
* **Published releases only:** The public release manifest excludes unpublished drafts, preventing premature release announcements in the application.

### Upgrade Notes

Upgrade the application images. This release adds no database migrations compared with v0.1.23.

Set `FRONTEND_URL` to the externally reachable Kuayle URL. The existing GitHub App needs Pull requests: Read and write and the Pull request webhook subscription; installations already using the documented permissions need no permission change. There is no historical PR backfill. After resolving a GitHub API or permission failure, redeliver the failed opened event from the app's webhook delivery page.

## What's Changed

* **Cycle actions menu fixed:** The three-dot menu on each cycle in the cycles list now opens, and offers edit, start, complete and delete. Older cycles have working actions too. Deleting a cycle asks for confirmation.
* **Cycle and project pages match the issues view:** Cycle and project detail pages now offer the same grouping, filters, list/board switcher, bulk actions and load-more as the team issues page. Issues open on the full issue page in both, instead of a side sheet on projects. Projects keep their Gantt view.
* **Easier issue management in cycles and projects:** *Add issues* opens a searchable picker that finds any issue in the team, not just the first 50. You can select several issues at once and retry any that fail. *New issue* is prefilled with the current cycle or project. *Remove from cycle/project* takes an issue out of the cycle or project without deleting it.
* **Clearer permissions and states:** Guests no longer see create, edit or delete actions on cycles and projects. Project deletion asks for confirmation, and the cycle can be edited from its detail page. Loading and error states and mobile layouts are improved, and cycle statuses and dates are fully translated.
* **Accurate project progress:** The progress number on project lists now matches the progress bar.

### Upgrade Notes

Update your application images. This release adds no database migrations, configuration changes or backend API changes.

## What's Changed

* **Issue version history:** Review recorded title and description edits from either issue view. Browse changes chronologically, see the editor and timestamp, and compare the complete before/after values in your selected app language. Descriptions include sanitized previews and an HTML source view.
* **Reliable history capture:** Content changes and their history now commit together. Failed saves leave no content-history entry, unchanged saves add no revision, and concurrent edits record the actual prior values. Property and automation updates preserve newer content. Private-team access rules continue to apply.
* **Security fixes:** Updated the Go toolchain and all Go image builders to 1.26.10, markdown-it to 14.3.3, and the application and marketing site's Vite dependencies to patched versions. The marketing site's cookie dependency, Caddy's compression library, and the IDE's bundled redirect library are also patched.

### Upgrade Notes

This release includes database migration 47. Back up the database and deploy the new backend together with its migration; do not keep older backend instances writing while the new history trigger is active. Existing recorded changes remain available, but unrecorded historical versions cannot be reconstructed. History from writes without an identified editor shows an unknown author. Version restoration is not included.

Update application images and rebuild/recreate updater and Dev Machine containers so they use the patched Go binaries. Source installations require Go 1.26.10 or newer. Rolling back migration 47 removes automatic capture while preserving history, including nullable author IDs.

**Pull request:** https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/70

## What's Changed

* **Security fixes:** Updated all Go build stages and Dev Machine agent toolchains to Go 1.26.9, addressing the HTTP, HTTP/2, TLS, and reverse-proxy vulnerabilities reported by the security workflow.
* **Patched networking dependencies:** Updated `golang.org/x/net` to 0.60.0 and its required companion modules in the backend and rebuilt Caddy with the same patched dependencies.
* **Broader security checks:** Security scans now run on every push to `main` and include the self-hosted updater image.

### Upgrade Notes

Update your application images. For source-based self-hosting, pull this release, rebuild the updater and Dev Machine images, and recreate affected containers so they use the patched binaries. Source installations require Go 1.26.9 or newer. This release adds no database migrations.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.1.19...v0.1.20

## What's Changed

* **Private teams:** Added privacy controls and membership-based access across issues, projects, cycles, comments, attachments, and real-time updates. Access is revoked when membership is removed; workspace owners and admins retain access. By @carbogninalberto in https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/67
* **More reliable navigation:** Temporary membership-check failures no longer redirect users or leave them stuck on the splash screen. Older failed requests also no longer override a successful retry. By @carbogninalberto in https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/pull/68
* **Safer self-hosted upgrades:** The updater stops backend writers before privacy migrations and keeps the backend stopped if a migration fails, preventing an older version from running against a partially migrated database.
* **Fixed Docker routing:** API requests, uploads, and health/readiness endpoints now reach the backend correctly instead of being intercepted by the frontend fallback.
* **Configurable build memory:** Docker UI builds now default to a configurable 4 GB Node heap.
* **Dependency fixes:** Updated `source-map-js` to address a denial-of-service flaw, refreshed vulnerable marketing-site build dependencies, and patched a code-server compression memory leak in the Dev Machines IDE image.
* **Updated self-hosting documentation:** Added private-team setup, legacy attachment handling, migration requirements, and downgrade guidance.

### Upgrade Notes

Existing teams remain public after upgrading. Enabling private teams introduces persistent workspace-wide restrictions: saved views, filtered/view-based public links, workspace export, AI expansion, outgoing webhooks, Dev Machines, and live presence are disabled—even if all teams are later made public or deleted.

Back up PostgreSQL and asset storage before upgrading. Apply migrations with backend writers stopped, and deploy the new backend and migrations together. See the [private-team documentation](https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle#private-teams) before enabling privacy.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.1.18...v0.1.19
